solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The best spot to discover where lions hang out — just the opposite

indicators.note: the opposite order is wanted, so the words of the phrase swap ends rather than staying as found

parts.note: a group of lions is a pride, so their haunt is the place of the pride

explanation.surface: A safari guide promises the best viewing spot, then admits it is the reverse of where the lions actually are.
explanation.walkthrough: Here it is the three words, not the letters, that change places: PLACE OF PRIDE becomes PRIDE OF PLACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Having pride of place means occupying the most prominent or honoured position, the top spot.

clue.text: Tumble to net

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to tumble to something is to grasp it at last
second meaning: to bring in money as profit from a sale

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a fall into a safety net; 'tumble to' is an informal phrase for suddenly understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both understanding something and converting assets into cash, so both senses fit one word.

clue.text: Novelist's daughter has one from Tel Aviv

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
a native of Tel Aviv is an Israeli; 'has' just sets it beside the abbreviation

explanation.surface: A writer's daughter is going out with someone from Tel Aviv.
explanation.walkthrough: Benjamin Disraeli, the Victorian Prime Minister, also wrote novels such as Sybil, so 'Novelist' is a fair if sly description.
explanation.definitionFit: Disraeli wrote a string of successful novels besides his political career, so he is an example of a novelist.

clue.text: Against Year 10 getting material for making cameos

parts.note: leaning on something is leaning against it
Y is the abbreviation for year
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A school complaint: Year 10 pupils are being handed materials for their drama cameos, and someone objects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cameos' suggests small acting parts; here they are carved jewellery pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded stone whose contrasting layers are carved into relief jewellery, a classic cameo material.

clue.text: Bemused prior to receiving the low-down from dad

indicators.note: the scrambled letters take something in, holding it inside them
someone bemused is muddled, so these letters come out in a muddled order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
gen is British slang for information, the low-down

explanation.surface: Someone is baffled before a parent gives them the full story.
explanation.definitionFit: A progenitor is a direct ancestor or parent, and a father is the most familiar example of one.

clue.text: Better going back into A&E quickly

indicators.note: one piece is placed into the other, ending up surrounded by it

parts.note: the letters A and E taken as written, with the ampersand dropped

indicators.note: something going back travels the other way, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it

explanation.surface: A patient recovering should not go back into Accident and Emergency in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British hospital casualty department, but here it is just two letters to wrap around.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace is a slightly literary adverb meaning at speed, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Grave words, essentially well-meaning, about father putting on weight

indicators.note: the essence of something is its heart, so only the central letter of the phrase is kept

parts.note: the central letter of the eleven letters of the phrase

indicators.note: as a fattening body puts weight around itself, the pieces go inside the word for weight

parts.note: pith means substance or weight, as in an argument with real pith

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A kindly memorial inscription mentions a father who had grown stout in later life.
explanation.walkthrough: Pith means substance or weight, as in a pithy remark. 'Grave' looks like the adjective solemn but is the noun, a burial place.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph is the inscription carved on a tombstone, literally words on a grave.

clue.text: Best to follow with piping hot cooked food

indicators.note: one piece is told to come after the others, so it is placed at the end

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with

indicators.note: cooked figures are fiddled or doctored, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
the cream of something is its best part

explanation.surface: A chef recommends serving the best things straight after a piping hot cooked meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piping hot' reads as one phrase, but the two words are separate pieces. 'Food' is a broad but fair definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Whipping cream is a high-fat cream sold for beating into peaks, an edible ingredient and so a kind of food.

clue.text: Denis, seconds away, failed to stop when uncertain

indicators.note: something that has failed has broken down, so the remaining letters are jumbled
something sent away is no longer there, so that letter is removed from the name

parts.note: the name taken as written
S is the abbreviation for seconds
to terminate is to stop or bring to an end

explanation.surface: A boxer called Denis, as the bell rings for 'seconds away', could not stop his opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seconds away' is the boxing call to start a round; here it tells you to remove the S from Denis.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeterminate means not fixed or not known exactly, so it is a close synonym of uncertain.

clue.text: Be informed of, for example, report

parts.note: to hear of something is to be informed of it
'say' introduces an example, just as 'for example' does

explanation.surface: Someone is told about something, for instance by a report.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearsay is information passed on by others rather than witnessed, which is report in the sense of rumour.

clue.text: Address in Ontario released

indicators.note: letters set free can scatter and settle in a new order

parts.note: the Canadian province's name taken as written

explanation.surface: A statement or postal address published in the Canadian province of Ontario.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' looks like a location in Ontario; it is a formal speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal public speech, and an address is a speech delivered to an audience.

clue.text: Trouble over stashing cocaine near back of sheep fold

indicators.note: being near means sitting alongside, so the pieces are placed side by side
the back of a word is its end, so only its last letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of the word

indicators.note: turned over, the word is read in the opposite direction
to stash something is to hide it away inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
C is drug slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: A farmer finds drugs hidden near the back of a sheep pen and senses trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheep fold' reads as a pen for sheep, but 'fold' is the definition, split from the sheep. A plica is an anatomical fold.
explanation.definitionFit: Plica is the anatomical term for a fold of skin or membrane, so it is a technical synonym.

clue.text: Committee member for England's foremost cricket side in 1750 for instance

indicators.note: the pieces sit in another word, which surrounds them

parts.note: a year such as 1750 is an example of a date

indicators.note: the foremost part of a word is its front, so only its first letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
in cricket the leg side is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs

explanation.surface: England's leading cricket team of 1750 is held up as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: D(E LEG)ATE. The leg side (also called on side) is one half of a cricket field, not a team.
explanation.definitionFit: A delegate is someone sent to represent others, as on a committee or at a conference.

clue.text: State categorically — this eventually follows when a girl's on speed

indicators.note: one piece follows the other, so it is placed directly after it
one piece sits on the next, so they are joined side by side

parts.note: 'as' can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: what happens eventually comes at the end, so the last letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of the word
Eve is a girl's name, the 's standing for 'is'
a rate is a speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A warning that consequences follow when a young woman takes amphetamines.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'follows' tells you the last letter of this comes after AS. 'Speed' looks like the drug but is simply a rate.
explanation.definitionFit: To asseverate is to declare solemnly and emphatically, so it is a formal synonym for stating firmly.

clue.text: Visionary Labour leader first to pursue plan to have unlimited credit

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so these pieces come after the plan

parts.note: an idea is a plan or scheme

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so just the first letter of the party name is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of the party name
1st, written as the numeral 1 read as I plus ST

indicators.note: without its limits, a word loses its outer letters and only the inside is kept

parts.note: buying on tick means buying on credit; tick without its outer letters

explanation.surface: A dreamy Labour leader's first plan is to borrow without limit.
explanation.walkthrough: TICK is British slang for credit; strip its ends for IC. 'First' becomes IST by reading the 1 of '1st' as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A visionary has lofty ideals and imagines how things could be, which is what being idealistic means.

clue.text: Originally exposed after an article by you many years ago

indicators.note: this piece comes after the other, so it is placed second

parts.note: 'the' is the definite article in grammar

indicators.note: what something was originally is how it began, so only its first letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A newspaper story exposing someone was published long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Thee is the old objective form of the pronoun, used in English centuries ago where we now say you.

clue.text: Unprepared, in retrospect, to design European fighting machine

indicators.note: retrospect means looking back, so the word is read from the end to the start

parts.note: raw recruits are unprepared ones
a plan is a design
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Looking back, the Europeans were ill-prepared to design a combat aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A warplane is a military aircraft built for combat, so it is a machine for fighting.

clue.text: Once more without a profit

indicators.note: without something means lacking it, so that letter is removed

parts.note: again means once more
the letter taken as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: Doing something again with nothing to show for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gain is something earned or acquired, so it is a straightforward synonym for profit.

clue.text: Animals lacking in strength left out sadly

indicators.note: the abbreviation for left is omitted, so that letter drops out

parts.note: limp means weak or lacking firmness
L is the abbreviation for left
alas is an exclamation of sorrow

explanation.surface: Weak animals abandoned, which is a sad thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Impalas are African antelopes, so they are an example of animals.

clue.text: A reminder from mother to ring joiner after more damage

indicators.note: to ring is to encircle, so one word surrounds the others

parts.note: mum is the British word for mother

indicators.note: this piece follows the other within the ring
damaged things are knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
and is a conjunction, a word that joins

explanation.surface: Mother leaves a note to call the carpenter after further damage to the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiner' suggests a carpenter, as it means in Britain; here it is a grammatical joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: A memorandum is a written note to help recall something, so it is literally a reminder.

clue.text: Force soldiers to run through river

indicators.note: passing through something puts it in the middle, so these pieces sit inside the river

parts.note: the Don is a river in Yorkshire and also in Scotland
RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of soldiers
to run is to go

explanation.surface: Troops are made to wade across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To dragoon someone is to coerce them into doing something, so it is a synonym of force as a verb.

clue.text: Made a complaint about return of unwelcome French queen

indicators.note: a return is a journey back, so the following words are read in reverse

parts.note: de trop is a French phrase used in English for unwanted or superfluous
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone protests at the unwanted homecoming of a French queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' looks like describing the queen; it belongs to 'unwelcome', pointing to the borrowed phrase de trop.
explanation.definitionFit: Reporting someone means making a formal complaint about them to an authority.

clue.text: Illingworth had a short one to manage getting out of bed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bowler's approach to the wicket, which for the off-spinner Ray Illingworth was brief
second reading: RUN for manage plus UP for out of bed

explanation.walkthrough: Ray Illingworth was an England cricket captain and spin bowler; spinners take only a few steps before bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-up is the approach a bowler takes before delivering the ball in cricket.

clue.text: Give reasons for taking off without Frank

indicators.note: taking something off removes it, so those letters go

parts.note: to explain is to give the reasons for something
ex is Latin for out of, so it means without

explanation.surface: Someone justifying a departure without someone called Frank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name; it is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain speaking is frank, candid speaking, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Talented government minister needing no introduction

indicators.note: without its introduction the name loses its opening letter

parts.note: Vince Cable was Business Secretary in the coalition government when this appeared

explanation.surface: A gifted minister so well known he needs no introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means skilled or competent, a direct synonym of talented.

clue.text: City worker included in short reference book

indicators.note: something included in another sits inside it
cut short, the book's name loses its last letter

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps used for reference
the worker ant is a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A city employee gets a mention in an abridged reference work.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlanta is the capital of the US state of Georgia, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Confirm wild animal has escaped

parts.note: a bear is a wild animal
an escaped animal is out

explanation.surface: A news flash confirming that a dangerous animal is on the loose.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear out a claim is to support it with evidence, so it means to corroborate.

clue.text: Most excellent gibe about embracing new object of worship

parts.note: supreme means of the highest excellence

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap your arms round, so one piece is held inside
turned about, the letters end up in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A superb taunt aimed at a newly worshipped idol.
explanation.definitionFit: The Supreme Being is God, the deity who is the focus of religious devotion.
